Commentary.Commentary: South Africa have 6 points in the bag and have a foot in the door for the next round. Bangladesh will be really disappointed as they have let it slip off their palms. Now, with just two points for them, the group D gets more interesting. That is all from this match. The next match is from Group C as Pakistan will take on Canada at the same venue. That game will begin on Tuesday, the 11th of June at 8 pm IST (2.30 pm GMT). You can however join us early for the build-up. Till then, goodbye and cheers!

Aiden Markram, the captain of South Africa says that everyone was going to be pretty nervous in this sort of a final over finish and sometimes you get over the line and sometimes you don't but it makes for great entertainment. On his crucial catch, he says that it was a matter of a meter or two and reckons they got a bit lucky at times and on Maharaj bowling the final over, he says that it depends on the situation and the pacers had to bowl the earlier overs. Adds that the partnership between David Miller and Heinrich Klaasen and is happy to see them doing well at crucial times.

Najmul Hossain Shanto, the captin of Bangladesh says they were nervous but they were hopeful that Jaker Ali will help win the match but this things happen in cicket. Feels they should have won the match but tells South Africa bowled well in the last couple of overs. Mentions Rishad Hossain is very good, he works hard and is showing his skills, says they are lucky to have him.

Heinrich Klaasen is the Player of the Match for his gritty batting performance. Klaasen starts by saying that it feels good that the boys got over the line. Adds that the wicket isn't great for stroke-play but they had good information from David Miller about the wicket from the last game and managed to put on a decent total. Mentions he and Miller had a One-Day mindset and wanted to shift gears after the 15th over which unfortunately didn't happen. Ends by saying that they have got three games out of the way, winning all of them and will now look forward to the next stage.
...Presentation next...

South Africa have virutally registered their names in the Super Eight but by no means they have played their best cricket yet. They have had to be really clutch in all three matches. Today as well, they registered a very low total as the batters failed yet again. South Africa were 23/4 but then came the match-winning partnership between David Miller and Heinrich Klaasen. The duo added 79 runs but South Africa failed to get the required finish in the fag end of the innings. However, the bowlers stepped up, kept chipping in with wickets regularly and it was in the last couple of overs where they really showed the grit to get the two points. Keshav Maharaj, in particularly showed his experience in the final over.

Aiden Markram took a huge, huge gamble by batting first on a slow, soft pitch! He did talked about how difficult it is to chase down totals and how important are the last 10 overs in the game. The Proteas bowlers showed a lot of character to defend such a lot total. However, it was not easy going for them when Towhid Hridoy and Mahmudullah were batting. Bangladesh were reeling at 50/4 at one stage and were in similar position to South Africa however, Towhid Hridoy and Mahmudullah came to the rescue and put on a solid stand of 44 runs before Hridoy was dismissed. Bangladesh still had Mahmudullah out there and they bet on him to chase it down. Mahmudullah, in the back of his mind made the decision to target Keshav Maharaj in the final over but his plan got wasted as he hammered a low full toss in the hands of Markram. He fell and the onus was on Jaker Ali but he too failed to hit the winning runs.

The Streak remains intact! It's 9-0 to South Africa in T20s and Bangladesh have to wait a little longer to get better of the Proteas. We have witnessed yet another low-scoring thriller in this year's World Cup. South Africa have successful defended their lowest total. How were the nerves there by Keshav Maharaj? Bowling the final over with just over 10 runs to play with, he did get away with a few full tosses but Maharaj was just good enough to get things done for his team.

Is that a no ball for height? No, it is fine and SOUTH AFRICA HAVE DONE IT! Keshav Maharaj lets slip of another delivery and ends up serving a very high full toss that angles quickly across the left-hander. The trajectory made it difficult to put away and Taskin Ahmed ends up slicing it away over the cover region for a single. The height is just about fine and South Africa have won by 4 runs and remain unbeaten in Men's T20Is against Bangladesh!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX RUNS NEEDED IN ONE DELIVERY! Taskin Ahmed walks out. Can he be the hero for Bangladesh?

Markram moves to his left from long on and takes it inches inside the ropes on the run and over his shoulder as well. What a moment and that could be the knockout blow for Bangladesh.

OUT! CAUGHT! Anrich Nortje picks up a wicket in his first over and that's a double whammy for South Africa. Nortje steams in from over the stumps and bangs it in short and quick at 146.6 clicks around off stump. Shakib Al Hasan looks to take it on and moves to the off side but gets rushed into the pull. Eventually, the ball goes nowhere and just pops up around short mid on and Aiden Markram takes the simplest of catches. Shakib's sluggish campaign continues.
Commentary.Howout: c Aiden Markram b Anrich Nortje
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.4: Anrich Nortje to Shakib Al Hasan, OUT! c Aiden Markram b Anrich Nortje.

Commentary.Commentary: Fractionally short again at 145-plus KPH and attacking the pads, Najmul Hossain Shanto flicks it down to fine leg and turns the strike over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.3: Anrich Nortje to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Just short of a good length, slanting it across from the leg stump line, Najmul Hossain Shanto stays watchful and blocks it late with soft hands.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.2: Anrich Nortje to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts with a length delivery, hurling it at the pads at almost 144 clicks, Shakib Al Hasan tucks the ball away through the mid-wicket region and gets off strike.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.1: Anrich Nortje to Shakib Al Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Anrich Nortje is into the attack.
Fuller one on the stumps, Najmul Hossain Shanto brings out the reverse sweep and nails it behind the man at point for a couple of easy runs.

Commentary.Commentary: This is tossed up at the stumps, Shakib Al Hasan skips down the pitch and drills it down to long off for a run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowled flatter and on the pads, Najmul Hossain Shanto with the paddle sweep behind square leg for another single.

Commentary.Commentary: Holds it back a touch and bowls it around off stump, Najmul Hossain Shanto leans forward and plays it back to the bowler.

Commentary.Commentary: Off the mark right away! Floated up from over the stumps and angling down leg, Shakib Al Hasan sweeps it down to fine leg and picks up a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Keshav Maharaj to Shakib Al Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shakib Al Hasan is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Gone first ball and Litton Das cannot believe it. Keshav Maharaj comes into the attack and begins from around the stumps, drifting it full onto middle and leg stump. Litton Das tries to back away and open up the off side but ends up smashing it straight to David Miller at short cover and he takes a sharp catch there. Soft dismisaal for Litton but South Africa will be ecstatic with that.
Commentary.Howout: c David Miller b Keshav Maharaj
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Keshav Maharaj to Litton Das, OUT! c David Miller b Keshav Maharaj.

Commentary.Commentary: A streaky single to end the Powerplay and Bangladesh are 29/1! Pitched up around the off stump, Litton Das looks to get forward and drive it away but gets an inside edge past the stumps and towards fine leg for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Kagiso Rabada to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowled from around the stumps and on a hard length outside off, Najmul Hossain Shanto taps the ball on the head and gets it away behind the man at backward point for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: Just back of a length and angling it across the off stump, Najmul Hossain Shanto stays back and dabs it away with and angled bat to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Kagiso Rabada to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Keeps bowling it on a hard length and at the stumps, Litton Das works it away in between mid on and mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Kagiso Rabada to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Up in the air but over the infield! Pitched up around off, not quite coming onto the bat, Litton Das splices it away over the cover region and picks up a couple of runs.

Commentary.Commentary: A length ball on the pads. Das nudges it to square leg for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Respect the good balls, hit the bad ones away! Bangladesh have got it right so far. Short in length and on the hips. Das pulls it behind square leg and it bounces right in front of the ropes.

Commentary.Commentary: Ohh no! Not a good place to get hit! Short of a length and on middle. Das looks to pull but the ball stays low and gets hit on the box.

Commentary.Commentary: A good length ball, outside off, Das hops and punches it to covers.

Commentary.Commentary: THREE RUNS! That's good running. Back of a length and on middle, Najmul Hossain Shanto pulls it through square leg. Slow outfield and Tristan Stubbs runs back and cuts it off. Three runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Litton Das walks in at number 3.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! There was definetly a sound. Tanzid Hasan is not sure if he nicked it and walks across to his skipper and has a chat but Najmul Hossain Shanto too has heared a sound here. Tanzid Hasan has to go. Kagiso Rabada has the final laugh! Short in length and around off, hits the deck hard and bowls it just outside off. Tanzid Hasan looks to cut but gets a faint edge to the keeper who makes no mistake.
